terra.problem: Saying the people are not confused or lost rules out possibilities the text does not address.
The toddler comparison is a scenario aimed at children, rather than the adult audience.
The explanation says deceit is leading the people away from God. The verse says they cling to deceit and refuse to return, but does not state that connection.
Full gallop and the horse not caring what is in front of it add details and an attitude to the comparison that the text does not give.
The passage does not say the horse is going at full speed or that nobody is reining it in.
Saying the thing in the people's hands had been bent suggests their copy of the Law was altered. The verse says the scribes' lying pen produced a deception, without specifying that.
The explanation says the wound is being covered up and equates the covering with the phrase about peace. The verse says the wound is dressed with very little care; it does not say it is concealed.
The explanation treats the harvest as already taken away, but God says He will take it away.
The voices propose fleeing; the text does not say they are already running. Nor does it say the fortified cities are the strongest places they know.
Calling this a big change from earlier implies a development in the same people's response that the passage does not establish.
The explanation presents the voices as different from the people described earlier, but the passage does not identify their relationship.
The verse says there was terror, not that it was loud.
The passage does not say the horses have not arrived. Dan's location in the far north is also a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The explanation adds claims about calming snakes and using tricks or music. The verse says only that these vipers cannot be charmed and will bite.
The explanation identifies who the 'you' addresses, but the verse does not explicitly identify the audience.
